name: Ondansetron
summary: A highly effective antiemetic for nausea and vomiting, especially when serotonin-mediated emesis is central to the problem.
good: Acute nausea/vomiting where serotonin receptor blockade is effective.
bad: Unreviewed QT-risk stacking or severe constipation-prone patients.
clinicalPearls: It is one of the cleanest symptom-relief antiemetics when QT risk is kept in view.
mechanism: Blocks 5-HT3 receptors in the gut and central vomiting pathways.
indications: Post-operative nausea, chemotherapy-related nausea, gastroenteritis-associated vomiting, and other acute nausea states.
interactionNotes: Other QT-prolonging drugs and serotonergic combinations deserve review.

warnings: Constipation and QT prolongation are the classic watch-outs.
